newsitem.title: UK: UK government reiterates privatisation commitment.
newsitem.headline: UK government reiterates privatisation commitment.

text.p: The British government on Thursday reiterated its commitment to its privatisation programme, promising further moves to free companies from state-ownership.
Speaking at a government sponsored conference, President of the Board of Trade, Ian Lang said that the possibilitities for privatisation in Britain were by no means exhausted.

"There are many areas of the public sector where private sector disciplines can benefit the general public. Our privatisation agenda goes on... Privatisation is not so much a programme as a way of life. There is more to be done."
The conference -- Privatisation: Setting Enterprise free -- was organised as a shop-window for the skills of British companies for overseas countries starting down the road of privatisation.

The privatisation programme in Britain - an integral part of the government's economic strategy - has seen over 50 major and several hundred smaller companies privatised since it came to power in 1979.

In October the Government said it planned to publish legislation to privatise National Air Traffic Services as early as possible in 1997 although it is still undecided whether to privatise its postal services.
But Lang said Britain had much to offer the rest of the world in terms of its own experiences over the past 17 years.
